key_insight: The paper shows that lattice surgery can be adapted to trivalent planar architectures, enabling logical entanglement with lower resource overhead than standard four-valent layouts.
engineering_relevance: This makes surface-code-based quantum processors more practical for hardware with only degree-3 connectivity, reducing qubit and gate requirements for scalable planar designs.
method: Develop scalable lattice-surgery circuit constructions for trivalent architectures.
Compare resource scaling against four-valent measurement-based lattice surgery.
Simulate logical performance for a fluxonium-qubit-based implementation.
evidence_signal: The authors report resource reductions of O(d) qubits and O(d) two-qubit gates, and simulations suggest up to about 25% improvement in logical fidelity at distance three.
watch_item: The reported gains are based on targeted simulations and distance-three performance, so larger-distance hardware validation is still needed.
paper_title: Towards logical entanglement creation in trivalent planar architectures
